{{Short description|Second theorem in extreme value theory}}
The '''Pickands–Balkema–de Haan theorem''' gives the asymptotic [[Cumulative distribution function|tail distribution]] of a [[random variable]] when its true distribution is unknown. It is often called the second theorem in [[extreme value theory]]. Unlike the first theorem (the [[Fisher–Tippett–Gnedenko theorem]]), which concerns the maximum of a sample, the Pickands–Balkema–de Haan theorem describes the values above a threshold.

The theorem owes its name to mathematicians [[James Pickands]], Guus Balkema, and [[Laurens de Haan]].

==Conditional excess distribution function==
For an unknown distribution function <math>F</math> of a random variable <math>X</math>, the Pickands–Balkema–de Haan theorem describes the conditional distribution function <math>F_u </math> of the variable <math>X </math> above a certain threshold <math>u</math>. This is the so-called conditional excess distribution function, defined as

: <math>F_u(\ y\ ) = \operatorname\mathbb{P}\!\Bigl\{\ X-u \leq y ~\vert~ X > u\ \Bigr\} = \frac{\ F(u+y) - F(u)\ }{\ 1 - F(u)\ } </math>

for <math>\ 0 \leq y \leq x_F - u\ ,</math> where <math>\ x_F\ </math> is either the finite or infinite right endpoint of the underlying distribution <math>\ F ~.</math> The modified function <math>\ F_u\ </math> describes the distribution of the excess value over a threshold <math>\ u\ ,</math> given that the threshold is exceeded.

==Statement==
Let <math>F_u</math> be the conditional excess distribution function. Pickands,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Iii |first=James Pickands |date=1975-01-01 |title=Statistical Inference Using Extreme Order Statistics |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-statistics/volume-3/issue-1/Statistical-Inference-Using-Extreme-Order-Statistics/10.1214/aos/1176343003.full |journal=The Annals of Statistics |volume=3 |issue=1 |doi=10.1214/aos/1176343003 |issn=0090-5364|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Balkema and [[Laurens de Haan|de Haan]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Balkema |first1=A. A. |last2=de Haan |first2=L. |date=1974-10-01 |title=Residual Life Time at Great Age |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-probability/volume-2/issue-5/Residual-Life-Time-at-Great-Age/10.1214/aop/1176996548.full |journal=The Annals of Probability |volume=2 |issue=5 |doi=10.1214/aop/1176996548 |issn=0091-1798|doi-access=free }}</ref> posed that for a large class of underlying distribution functions <math>F</math>, and large <math>u</math>, <math>F_u</math> is well approximated by the [[generalized Pareto distribution]], in the following sense. Suppose that there exist functions <math>a(u), b(u)</math>, with <math>a(u)>0</math> such that <math>F_u(a(u) y+ b(u) )</math> as <math> u \rightarrow \infty</math> converge to a non-degenerate distribution, then such limit is equal to the generalized Pareto distribution:

: <math>F_u(a(u) y+ b(u)) \rightarrow G_{k, \sigma} (y),\text{ as }u \rightarrow \infty</math>,

where
*<math>G_{k, \sigma} (y)= 1-(1+ky/\sigma)^{-1/k} </math>,  if <math>k \neq 0</math>
*<math>G_{k, \sigma} (y)= 1-e^{-y/\sigma} </math>,  if <math>k = 0.</math>

Here ''&sigma;''&nbsp;>&nbsp;0, and ''y''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;0 when ''k''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;0 and 0&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''y''&nbsp;≤&nbsp;&minus;''&sigma;''/''k'' when ''k''&nbsp;<&nbsp;0. These special cases are also known as  

*[[Exponential distribution]] with [[expected value|mean]] <math>\sigma</math>,  if ''k''&nbsp;=&nbsp;0,
*[[Uniform distribution (continuous)|Uniform distribution]] on <math>[0,\sigma]</math>,  if k = -1,
* [[Pareto distribution]], if ''k''&nbsp;>&nbsp;0.

The class of underlying distribution functions <math>F</math> are related to the class of the distribution functions <math>F</math> satisfying the [[Fisher–Tippett–Gnedenko theorem]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Balkema |first1=A. A. |last2=de Haan |first2=L. |date=1974-10-01 |title=Residual Life Time at Great Age |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-probability/volume-2/issue-5/Residual-Life-Time-at-Great-Age/10.1214/aop/1176996548.full |journal=The Annals of Probability |volume=2 |issue=5 |doi=10.1214/aop/1176996548 |issn=0091-1798|doi-access=free }}</ref> 

Since a special case of the generalized Pareto distribution is a power-law, the Pickands–Balkema–de Haan theorem is sometimes used to justify the use of a power-law for modeling extreme events.

The theorem has been extended to include a wider range of distributions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Papastathopoulos |first1=Ioannis |last2=Tawn |first2=Jonathan A. |date=2013 |title=Extended Generalised Pareto Models for Tail Estimation |journal=Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference |volume=143 |issue=1 |pages=131–143 |doi=10.1016/j.jspi.2012.07.001|arxiv=1111.6899 |s2cid=88512480 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lee |first1=Seyoon |last2=Kim |first2=Joseph H. T. |date=2019-04-18 |title=Exponentiated generalized Pareto distribution: Properties and applications towards extreme value theory |url=https://doi.org/10.1080/03610926.2018.1441418 |journal=Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods |volume=48 |issue=8 |pages=2014–2038 |doi=10.1080/03610926.2018.1441418 |arxiv=1708.01686 |s2cid=88514574 |issn=0361-0926}}</ref> While the extended versions cover, for example the normal and log-normal distributions, still continuous distributions exist that are not covered.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Smith |first1=Richard L. |url=https://rls.sites.oasis.unc.edu/s834-2020/ExtremeValues.pdf |title=Extreme Values |last2=Weissman |first2=Ishay |edition=draft 2/27/2020}}</ref>
